concepts.name: Origins and Triggers of the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22)
key_dimensions: Dual triggers: Rowlatt Act (1919), Jallianwala Bagh massacre AND Khilafat grievances — UPSC trap: distinguishing primary vs. secondary causes
Role of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) as a backdrop of disillusionment
Gandhi's shift from constitutionalism to mass agitation: the philosophical break
Why 1920 and not earlier — organizational readiness of the INC post-Lucknow Pact

concepts.name: Nagpur Session of INC (1920): Formal Adoption of NCM
key_dimensions: Significance of the Nagpur Session vs. the Calcutta Special Session (September 1920) — UPSC trap: which session formally launched NCM
Reorganization of Congress on linguistic lines — structural transformation often overlooked
Gandhi's ascendancy over Tilak's faction and the 'moderate' dissenters like Jinnah
The resolution of 'Swaraj within one year' — promise, context, and failure implications

concepts.name: The Khilafat Movement and its Merger with NCM
key_dimensions: Role of Ali Brothers (Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali) — their relationship with Gandhi
Hindu-Muslim unity as a strategic objective vs. its fragility — UPSC often tests why the unity collapsed
The Ottoman Caliphate question: why Indian Muslims cared and the Treaty of Sèvres (1920)
Abolition of the Caliphate by Kemal Ataturk (1924) — how an external event ended the movement's religious plank

concepts.name: Programme of Non-Cooperation: Constructive vs. Obstructive Elements
key_dimensions: Four-stage programme: surrender of titles, boycott of councils/courts/schools, boycott of foreign goods, non-payment of taxes — sequence and which stages were actually implemented
UPSC trap: Non-payment of taxes was NOT universally called — Gandhi was selective about this stage
Constructive programme: promotion of swadeshi, charkha, national schools, panchayats
Difference between the NCM programme and the Civil Disobedience Movement programme — a classic comparison question

concepts.name: Boycott of Legislative Councils and the Swarajist Response
key_dimensions: Congress's decision to boycott the reformed councils under Montford Reforms
The Swarajist Party (1923) — Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das's 'council entry' strategy as a direct reaction to NCM's failure
UPSC trap: Swarajists formed AFTER NCM was suspended — the cause-effect relationship
Arguments for and against council entry — the 'wrecking from within' doctrine

concepts.name: Boycott of Educational Institutions and National Alternatives
key_dimensions: Establishment of national institutions: Jamia Millia Islamia (1920), Kashi Vidyapith, Gujarat Vidyapith — UPSC loves institutional founding dates
Response of students vs. professionals — uneven participation in the boycott
Long-term impact: creation of a parallel education ecosystem
C.R. Das's sacrifice — giving up a lucrative legal practice as a symbol of the lawyers' boycott

concepts.name: Role of the Charkha and Swadeshi in NCM
key_dimensions: Charkha as both an economic tool and a symbol of self-reliance — Gandhi's philosophical reasoning
Bonfire of foreign cloth — mass mobilization technique and its psychological impact
UPSC trap: Swadeshi as a concept predates NCM (Swadeshi Movement 1905) — what was new about Gandhi's swadeshi
Tagore's critique of burning foreign cloth as 'destructive' vs. Gandhi's defence

concepts.name: Chauri Chaura Incident (February 1922) and Withdrawal of NCM
key_dimensions: Facts: Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur district, UP — mob burned a police chowki killing 22 policemen
Gandhi's unilateral withdrawal decision — reactions from within Congress (Nehru, C.R. Das were in jail and opposed)
UPSC trap: The movement was withdrawn NOT because it failed but because of Gandhi's moral principle of non-violence
Debate: Was withdrawal strategically premature? — this is a recurring analytical question

concepts.name: Gandhi's Arrest and Trial (1922): The 'Great Trial'
key_dimensions: Charged under Section 124A IPC (sedition) — same section used against Tilak earlier
Gandhi's famous statement in court: accepted guilt and demanded the highest penalty — a masterclass in moral politics
Judge Broomfield's tribute to Gandhi — a unique moment in colonial legal history
Sentenced to 6 years, released in 1924 after appendicitis surgery — UPSC tests the year of release

concepts.name: Mass Participation: New Social Groups Entering Nationalist Politics
key_dimensions: Peasants (especially in Awadh/UP), urban workers, students, women — the broadening of the nationalist base
Eka Movement (UP) and Mappila (Moplah) Rebellion (1921) — allied but distinct movements that UPSC uses to test cause-effect
UPSC trap: Mappila Rebellion started as anti-landlord/anti-British but turned communal — Congress's discomfort
Women's participation: first large-scale entry of women into public agitation — link to later Civil Disobedience

concepts.name: The Moplah (Mappila) Rebellion (1921): Context and Controversy
key_dimensions: Background: Muslim peasant-tenants in Malabar against Hindu landlords and British authority
Initial phase aligned with NCM/Khilafat; later communal violence against Hindus — the turning point
UPSC trap: Often confused as purely part of NCM — it was a parallel, partly autonomous agrarian revolt
Annie Besant's criticism vs. Gandhi's initial ambiguity — tests knowledge of Congress's internal debates

concepts.name: Akali Movement (Gurdwara Reform Movement) and its Relation to NCM
key_dimensions: Mahant control of Sikh shrines — the Gurdwara Reform Movement (1920–25) as a parallel mobilization
UPSC trap: Akali Movement was NOT part of NCM but coincided with it — Congress supported it morally
Guru Ka Bagh confrontation (1922) — passive resistance inspired by Gandhian methods
Outcome: Sikh Gurdwaras Act (1925) — a rare legislative success during the NCM period

concepts.name: Gandhi's Concept of Swaraj in the Context of NCM
key_dimensions: 'Swaraj within one year' — what Gandhi meant (moral regeneration + political freedom) vs. popular expectation
Hind Swaraj (1909) as the ideological foundation — continuity and evolution of the concept
UPSC trap: Gandhi's Swaraj was not just political independence but civilizational transformation — often confused with Dominion Status demand
Why the 'one year' promise became a political liability after 1922

concepts.name: Role of the Press and Propaganda in NCM
key_dimensions: Gandhi's newspapers: Young India and Navajivan — medium of direct communication with masses
Seditious writings as a legal tool by the British — how press prosecutions worked
UPSC trap: Young India was in English, Navajivan in Gujarati — language choices were strategic
Role of vernacular press in regional mobilization — often tested in state-specific questions

concepts.name: British Response to NCM: Repression and Political Concessions
key_dimensions: Mass arrests of leaders: C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Lajpat Rai, Gandhi — strategic timing of arrests
UPSC trap: The British did NOT make major political concessions during NCM — contrast with post-CDM concessions
The 'exhaustion strategy' of the colonial government — waiting out the movement
Difference in British response to NCM vs. Civil Disobedience Movement — a classic comparison

concepts.name: Tilak vs. Gandhi: Ideological Transition in Congress Leadership
key_dimensions: Bal Gangadhar Tilak died in August 1920 — the vacuum that enabled Gandhi's dominance
Tilak's approach: constitutional agitation + Hindu revivalism vs. Gandhi's non-violent mass civil disobedience
UPSC trap: Gandhi was NOT anti-Tilak — he acknowledged Tilak as his guru in the political sense
The shift from the 'Extremist-Moderate' binary to the Gandhian framework as a new paradigm

concepts.name: NCM and the Reorganization of the Indian National Congress
key_dimensions: Transformation of Congress from an elite debating society to a mass organization with a ₹4 crore fund and defined membership fee (4 annas)
Linguistic reorganization of provincial Congress committees — administrative decentralization
UPSC trap: The 4-anna membership was meant to democratize Congress — its actual vs. intended impact
Working Committee established as the executive body — structural legacy that survived independence

concepts.name: Outcomes and Legacy of the Non-Cooperation Movement
key_dimensions: What was achieved: mass politicization, Hindu-Muslim unity (temporary), establishment of parallel institutions, demonstration of India's capacity for organized resistance
What was NOT achieved: Swaraj, reversal of Rowlatt Act, Khilafat restoration — UPSC trap on measuring 'success'
Long-term legacy: established the template for CDM (1930) and Quit India (1942) — evolution of Gandhian methods
Nehru's reflection: NCM as the first movement that made the masses feel they were actors in history, not spectators

concepts.name: NCM vs. Civil Disobedience Movement: Key Structural Differences
key_dimensions: NCM: refusal to cooperate with the state; CDM: active breaking of specific laws — conceptual distinction UPSC frequently tests
NCM had no specific demand trigger; CDM had the 11-point ultimatum to Viceroy Irwin
Geographical spread: CDM was broader and more sustained; NCM collapsed after Chauri Chaura
Role of women: significantly larger in CDM — evolution of mass participation across movements
